Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Reform UK 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Immigration
The party proposes freezing non-essential immigration, leaving the European Convention on Human Rights, and implementing offshore processing for asylum seekers arriving illegally. Foreign criminals would face immediate deportation after serving sentences. A 20% National Insurance rate would apply to foreign workers (exempting healthcare workers and small businesses), with proceeds funding apprenticeships. Student visa rules would bar dependents, and a 5-year residency requirement would apply before claiming benefits.

## Economy
Personal tax changes include raising the income tax threshold to £20,000 (removing 7 million people from income tax), cutting stamp duty (0% below £750k), abolishing inheritance tax for estates under £2 million, and reducing fuel duty by 20p per litre. For businesses, corporation tax would drop to 15% by year three, the VAT threshold would rise to £150,000, IR35 rules would be abolished, and business rates eliminated for high street SMEs. An online delivery tax of 4% would apply to large multinationals.

## Public Spending
Proposed savings include stopping Bank of England interest payments on QE reserves (£35 billion annually), requiring 5% efficiency savings across departments (£50 billion), halving foreign aid (£6 billion saved), and improving tax collection.

## NHS
Plans include tax exemptions for frontline staff, 20% tax relief on private healthcare, and a voucher system allowing patients to access private care if NHS waiting times exceed specified limits (3 days for GPs, 3 weeks for consultants, 9 weeks for operations). Weekend operating theatre use would be mandated.

## Energy
The manifesto proposes scrapping Net Zero targets and renewable energy subsidies, fast-tracking North Sea oil and gas licences, exploring shale gas, and developing small modular nuclear reactors.

## Law and Order
Proposals include recruiting 40,000 new police officers, implementing zero-tolerance policing, building 10,000 new detention places, mandatory life sentences for repeat violent offenders, and reopening magistrates' courts.

## Education
Changes include curriculum reviews emphasising British history, banning gender identity teaching in schools, 20% tax relief on independent school fees, scrapping student loan interest, and restricting undergraduate numbers.

## Benefits
The party proposes a two-strike rule requiring job acceptance within four months or after two offers, with benefits withdrawn for non-compliance. Face-to-face assessments would replace remote evaluations.

## Defence
Spending would increase to 3% of GDP within six years, with a pay review for armed forces personnel and a dedicated veterans ministry.

## Housing and Infrastructure
Plans include fast-tracking brownfield development, prioritising local residents for social housing, scrapping HS2, banning ULEZ zones, and creating a 50% public ownership model for utilities.

## Constitutional Reform
Proposals include leaving the ECHR, reforming the House of Lords, restricting postal voting, and holding a referendum on proportional representation.

## Funding
Total projected savings: £150 billion annually. Total projected costs: £141 billion annually. Additional growth assumptions project £10 billion in extra tax revenue.
